text:
sasha: quick spike update — canary shows nondeterministic evict+refetch loops after leader failover. suspect the handoff leaves different nodes with different "recency" views. i prototyped a tiny ticketing scheme: attach a 128-bit ticket to prefix residency so we have deterministic ordering across nodes during transfers.

mike: sketch please. is ticket global-monotonic or node-local?

sasha: node-local monotonic counter + node id (Ticket {node, counter}). when issuing ownership the node stamps the residency. eviction comparator uses (access_epoch, ticket) so recent accesses win; ticket is tie-break to avoid random ordering across handoffs.

anna: how do you prevent an old ticket from keeping a stale prefix alive forever if the new owner never bumps it?

sasha: add access_epoch (u64) bumped on access. eviction compares access_epoch first, then ticket. also soft-pin window for freshly transferred prefixes to avoid immediate eviction.

jordan: rehydrate concern: background rehydration could create duplicates or lower-priority copies. any plan?

sasha: background fills must request a ticket from the owner when converting transient->resident. otherwise they mark record transient and won't compete with resident entries.

mike: crash/recovery: what if a node restarts — its counters reset and you get lower tickets that look older but are actually new?

sasha: nodes publish tombstones with last-issued counter on restart. other nodes treat tickets with counter < tombstone_min[node] as expired; tombstone bumps the minimum so old counters don't confuse ordering.

anna: concurrent handoff + eviction race is scary. need handshake.

sasha: handshake: source marks residency TRANSFERRING with last_ticket, dest pulls and replies ACK with new ticket, then source clears after ACK. eviction defers if TRANSFERRING set or times out.

jordan: how's access_epoch maintained cheaply? global increments will be hot.

sasha: per-shard relaxed epoch counter — fast per-core increments, periodic compaction to a shard-level epoch. we don't need perfect timestamps, just coarse recency buckets.

mike: rollout strategy?

sasha: phased: (1) advertise fields in records but keep old comparator, (2) collect telemetry on post-handoff refetchs, (3) opt-in by shard flag, (4) flip default when stable.

anna: telemetry to capture: refetchs-per-handoff, post-failover tail latency, eviction churn. tests: unit comparator tests, tombstone recovery tests, chaos leader-failover+rehydrate+evict under load.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: CI job kv-cache/evict-ticket-sims is flaky; 2/3 seeds passed recently, one failed. https://ci.internal/12345

mike: thanks infra-bot. one more thing: counter wrap or huge node counts? 64-bit counters + node id should be safe; tombstones help defend against any odd wrap.

anna: ok file an RFC with sketches, API, tests and rollout. also include perf microbench for access_epoch bump cost.

sasha: already drafting RFC. will post link here when ready. :thumbsup:
